source_locator: R173: Einsatz and table of 1944, 10 November row; R434: p. 395
current_activity: The Twenty-fifth Army is formed in the Netherlands from the Armed Forces Commander Netherlands staff, under Army Group H
notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, entry on the Twenty-fifth Army: "Die 25. Armee bzw. das Armeeoberkommando 25 wurde am 10. November 1944 in den Niederlanden durch den OB West aufgestellt"; "Die Armee unterstand der Heeresgruppe H"; CMH Siegfried Line Campaign ch. 17 p. 395: "headquarters of the Armed Forces Commander Netherlands (General Christiansen), which took over the sector, called itself Fifteenth Army". Event definition: the formation date of 10 November in the Lexikon; CMH places the deception takeover of the sector at the time of the Fifth Panzer Army relief of 15 November. Event support: two source families (Lexikon for the day, CMH for the deception); the place is approximate. Location: Utrecht with a precision of 50 km, a representative point for the Netherlands; neither source names the headquarters place. Location approximate: a representative point for the Netherlands. Location support: both sources name only the Netherlands. Commander: General der Flieger Friedrich Christiansen. Opponents: Second British Army and Canadian First Army. Context: Until 16 December 1944 the Lexikon says the army used the cover designation AOK 15 to hide the move of the real Fifteenth Army to the Aachen area, which CMH describes in the same terms.

current_activity: Blumentritt leaves the Twenty-fifth Army on 28 March for the First Parachute Army
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 14 p. 302: "until General Blumentritt could be released from the Twenty-fifth Army to assume command on the 28th"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 25. Armee, commanders: "29. Januar 1945 General der Infanterie Günther Blumentritt m.F.b. 21. März 1945 Generaloberst Johannes Blaskowitz". Event definition: CMH gives 28 March for Blumentritt leaving; the Lexikon gives 21 March for Blaskowitz as commander and 30 March for Kleffel. Event support: two source families (CMH and the Lexikon, Tessin) that differ on the days. Location: Utrecht with a precision of 50 km, a representative point for the Netherlands, as on earlier rows of the Netherlands armies; neither source names the headquarters place. Location approximate: a representative point for the Netherlands. Location support: both sources name Holland only. Commander: General der Infanterie Günther Blumentritt. Opponents: British Second and Canadian First Armies. Context: The Lexikon list gives Blaskowitz as commander from 21 March and Kleffel from 30 March, which does not match CMH, where Blumentritt stays until 28 March; the difference is not resolved here.
